dialogue.Introduction: Oh, hello there, @! I'm the Mechanic, though up here everyone just calls me Robin. I took over the carpenter's shop on the mountain and I've been elbow deep in gears ever since. Mind the springs on the floor, alright?$h
dialogue.Mon: Monday already? The gears never sleep, so I don't either. Mind the wire by the door.
dialogue.Tue: Tuesday means oiling every hinge in this shop. Left alone they squeak like a grumpy goat.
dialogue.Wed: Wednesday. The Steampunker wants a new boiler again. I keep telling her the last one still has a dent from the ceiling.$u
dialogue.Thu: Thursday is inventory day. Bolts, bolts and more bolts. Thrilling, I know.
dialogue.Fri: Friday! The mine trolley always sticks on Fridays. If you're passing the cart, grab me some Iron Bars.
dialogue.Sat: Saturday, and the whole valley is out in the sun. I'd rather be under a machine, but I do love a good walk up this mountain.$h
dialogue.Sun: Sunday is my rest day. Mostly. There's always a clock somewhere that needs winding.
dialogue.Mon2: Back again? Fine, you can hold the lantern while I work. Don't drop it on the saw.$h
dialogue.Tue2: If you see a bent pipe lying about, don't kick it. That's a steam valve, and it has feelings.
dialogue.Mon4: Oh, @, you're becoming a regular up here. I'll admit I look forward to your visits more than I let on.$l
dialogue.Tue4: My bolt bin rattled all night, and I thought of you. Silly, I know. Here, want to try turning this crank?$h
dialogue.Wed4: Did you know I built my first contraption from a broken spoon and a bicycle wheel? My teachers were not impressed.$h
dialogue.Thu4: I like having someone to test my gadgets on, @. Most folks just stare at them and walk away.$h
dialogue.Fri4: The trolley is fixed for another week, thanks to your help with the rope. I owe you a pie, at least.$h
dialogue.Sat4: You know what I love about valley folk? Everyone brings a slice of their own weather with them.$h
dialogue.Sun4: Sundays are nicer with company. Stay for a cup of tea while the kettle whistles, will you?$h
dialogue.Mon6: Anything broken on your farm, you tell me first. I'd rather fix a sprinkler than watch a crop wilt.$h
dialogue.Thu6: I used to hide in the workshop when the goblins came through. These days I'm the one bringing gadgets out to meet them.$h
dialogue.Fri6: You keep finding me in the mess and never complain. I like that about you.$h
dialogue.Sat6: Out with it, then. What's the most useless machine you've ever owned? Mine is a clock that runs backward.$h
dialogue.Sun6: I made a little wind chime that sings when you whistle near it. Come by after supper and I'll show you.$h
dialogue.Mon8: I never told anyone this, but as a kid I took apart the town hall clock. My mother cried, then bought me a toolbox the very next day.$l
dialogue.Tue8: Sometimes the shop gets too quiet, and I hear every old gear groaning. Having you here makes the noise feel friendly.$l
dialogue.Wed8: The Steampunker and I argue all the time, but she's family to me. I wouldn't trade that for a dozen clean workshops.$h
dialogue.Thu8: I was scared when I first arrived here. A new town, a new shop, a house with no one to share it. You made it feel like home.$l
dialogue.Fri8: If I ever stop fixing things, I'd still want you around to tell me when my hair looks like a rat's nest.$h
dialogue.Sat8: Would you believe I'm happiest when a machine finally hums right? It's like a song, and you're the one who taught me to listen.$l
dialogue.Sun8: The farm is my favorite project, @. Every field, every fence, every gear you oil. I hope you know how much it means to me.$l
dialogue.Wed2: Careful with the blue fuel can. It's flammable and it smells like sunshine, which makes it dangerous.$h
dialogue.Wed10: We have been through so many breakdowns together. The gears are fine now, and so am I.$l
dialogue.Fri10: Promise me you'll always come up the mountain when something breaks. Even if it's just your heart. I can weld that too.$l
dialogue.Sun10: This shop wasn't a home until you walked in. Gears, grease and all, I'm glad you're here.$l
dialogue.spring_Tue: Spring always makes the shop damp and the kettle sulky. Still, the mountain air is lovely this time of year.
dialogue.summer_Sat: The summer heat makes the gears seize up. Come by with cold water and I'll tell you how to fix my fan.$h
dialogue.fall_Mon: Autumn leaves blow straight into my workshop. I've started sweeping twice a day, and still they come.
dialogue.winter_Sun: Snow piles up on the shop roof and the chimney coughs the whole time. Warm yourself by the forge, @.$h
dialogue.winter_Fri8: The cold makes the best ideas come, @. Last night I designed a heater that runs off coal and mostly stays put.$h
dialogue.spring_13: The Egg Festival is coming, and I've built a little egg-tapping machine. I promise it's safe, probably.$h
dialogue.fall_15: Harvest season is busy, but I always find time to walk the lanes and wave at the farmers.$h
dialogue.winter_20: Quiet winter days are good for building. I'm working on something new, and it's almost done.$h
dialogue.summer_3: Summer mornings are for tinkering on the porch. The birds like my wind chimes more than I do.
dialogue.summer_Mon: The mine's rails are hot enough to fry eggs this week. Don't tell the Dwarf I said so.
dialogue.winter_Thu: Cold metal is brittle, so I keep everything warm before I use it. Good habit for people too.
dialogue.spring_Sun: Spring is the season for new projects. I've already started three, and only one is on fire.$h

rainy: Rain on the mountain roof sounds just like a clockwork drum. I'd say it's relaxing, but the puddles keep ruining my wiring.

situations.eye: The big eyeball in the sky is gone, @. Good riddance. Those lenses were scratched anyway.$h
situations.evilBoss: Something big and nasty fell in the caves last night. My wrenches are still rattling from it.$u
situations.skeletron: Skeletron is down! The dungeon is open and the Old Man is free. The Clothier is buying a round for everyone at the saloon, so mind your coin.$h
situations.queenBee: The Queen Bee is finally gone. The honey smell has nearly worn out of my overalls, bless it.$h
situations.hardmode: The Wall of Flesh has fallen and hardmode has begun. Everything in the caves got meaner overnight, so keep your gear oiled.$u
situations.mechs: One of the mechanical bosses was smashed last night. Beautiful metal and a terrible mess. I'm already sorting the parts.$h
situations.plantera: Plantera is defeated! The jungle temple is open now, and I want every vine cut back for the sake of my gears.$h
situations.golem: The Golem is down, so the temple idols can stop glaring at me. I'll sleep better tonight.$h
situations.cultist: The Lunatic Cultist fell and the celestial pillars appeared in the sky. Go take a look before the sky gets stranger.$u
situations.moonLord: The Moon Lord is gone. I didn't know the sky could be this quiet until last night.$u
situations.goblins: A goblin army came marching through and got sent packing. The Goblin Tinkerer grumbled all morning about the cleanup.$a
situations.pirates: Pirates came up the shore last night and were chased off. Their ship still has a cannon I would love to take apart.$h
situations.frostLegion: The Frost Legion came for the valley last night. Cold snowmen with real knives. We held the line, mostly.$u
situations.martians: Martians! Ray guns and flying saucers over the farm last night. I wanted to be frightened, but I was too busy taking notes.$u
situations.bloodMoon: There was a blood moon last night and the monsters came out in droves. Keep a lamp by the door, @.$s
situations.eclipse: The sun went dark last night in a solar eclipse and all my clocks went haywire. Still, what a sight.$u
situations.party: The Party Girl is throwing a party today. I already set my best party hat on the workbench. Don't tell her, but she's worse with tools than I am.$h

festivals.spring13: Happy Egg Festival, @! I brought my egg-tapping machine. Please do not let the Party Girl near the crank.$h
festivals.spring24: Flower Dance! I'd dance with you, but my boots squeak on the polished floor. Watch your toes.$h
festivals.summer11: For the Luau I've put a copper pot in the soup. Mostly so it can be heated, which is more than my lunch can say.$h
festivals.summer28: The Dance of the Moonlight Jellies on the beach is my favorite night of the year. The jellies glow, the gears sparkle.$h
festivals.fall16: Stardew Valley Fair! I have a new gadget on display in the grange. It spins, it whistles and it has a tiny flag on top.$h
festivals.fall27: Spirit's Eve! I put some creaky gears in the maze. Watch out for the ticking, it is not a ghost. Probably.$u
festivals.winter8: Festival of Ice! I'm entering the ice fishing contest with a heater I built myself. Cheating? Only a little.$h
festivals.winter25: Feast of the Winter Star! I wrapped my gift with wire and tiny wrenches. Open it carefully, @.$h

loved.text: A wrench, a cog and a shiny bar of metal, all in one afternoon? You've made my whole week, @. Now, let's see what this little beauty can do.$h

liked.text: Ooh, parts! Some wire and a clock piece. Good taste, @. I can use these right away.$h

neutral.text: Thanks, @. That's a nice little thing. I'll find a place for it on the shelf.

disliked.text: Oh... this isn't something I can use. Honestly, it's just clutter on my workbench, @.$a

hated.text: Slime? Bat wing? Junk? Put that away, @. My shop is not a rubbish heap, and I have feelings about it.$a

events.after: Careful with that spring on the way out, it has a temper.

steps.say: Oh! @, hello. Mind the gears on the floor, they bite.$u
Name is Robin, but up here everyone calls me the Mechanic. I keep this shop running and the Steampunker's lab next door, which she keeps blowing up.$h
I can fix nearly anything with a wrench and a bit of wire. Here, have a look at this lever I rebuilt last week.$h

steps.question: What do you fix on your farm?

answers.reply: Sprinklers are lovely little machines. Bring them by and I'll tune them for you.$h

answers.text: Nothing, I just watch the crops grow.
answers.reply: Hmph. Watching things grow is a job for scarecrows.$a

steps.say: Anyway, that wire is for you. Keep it away from the stove and you'll be fine.$h

events.after: If you hear a whistling up in the pines, that's just my rocket rig.

steps.say: @! Fancy meeting you up here by the old quarry. I come to test my rocket rig. Mostly the rockets go up, mostly.$h
Mind where you stand. The wind up here blows my hat into the pines every second day.$h
The pines hum when the wind is right. My mother said I was born listening to machines, and the trees hum too.$s
I came up here after the shop sat empty for years. Nobody wanted the sawdust and the ghost of an old saw.#$b#Working with my hands keeps the quiet thoughts away.$s

steps.question: Do the pines ever talk back?

answers.reply: Then we're two of a kind. Fine company, you are.$h

answers.text: They sound like a broken fan to me.
answers.reply: Ha. A broken fan is still a fan, and I'll fix it one day.$a

steps.say: Thanks for listening, @. It's nice to have someone who doesn't think I'm mad for talking to tree sap.$h

events.after: Don't let the Steampunker talk you into standing near the boiler again.

steps.say: Oh, @! Perfect timing. Come see what the Steampunker did to my workbench.$u
It was an experiment! The little boiler ran on sparks for a whole minute.$h
A whole minute of smoke and singed eyebrows, and you call that science?$a
Oh, I was only joking. You two are the only people in town who understand a good gear ratio.$h

steps.question: Want to help build something loud?

answers.reply: Loud is exactly what I hoped you'd say.$h

answers.text: No, I'd rather keep my eyebrows.
answers.reply: Sensible. The boiler will still be waiting for you.$s

steps.say: This is my favorite bench. The Clockwork Assault Rifle is one of my designs, and most folks never even know it.$h
The lamps make everything look like a machine at night. Good thing I like the dark.$h
My dad was a mechanic too, back in a mining town far from here. He taught me a broken thing isn't finished until it works again.$s
I think that's why I stayed in the valley. Everyone here gets a second chance, even a rusty old carpenter's shop.$h
Let me walk you back. The mine trolley runs late and I don't want you lost in the dark.$h

steps.question: What do you want most from life?

answers.text: A quiet farm and good friends.
answers.reply: That's a fine dream. I'll help you keep the fences straight.$h
Ha! Then be careful. Treasure always has a trap, and I always have a fix.$h

steps.say: Goodnight, @. Rest well. Machines run better when their minds are calm.$h

events.after: Your farm is my favorite machine in the valley. Don't tell the others.

steps.say: @, your farm is the best machine in the valley. Every row straight, every sprinkler humming.$u
Do you know how rare it is to find something that works this well? I used to think all things had a breaking point.$s
Then I met folks who stayed with the broken things and fixed them. You taught me that, you know.$h

steps.question: Should we build a new mailbox or keep the old one?

answers.reply: Together. That's a deal I'll sign in grease.$h

answers.text: Keep the old one, it has character.
answers.reply: Character! It has more rust than character, but I agree.$h

steps.say: Thanks for letting me see your fields, @. Ideas always come easier when I see something grow.$h
